protocol: Predictions recorded before any discipline-ablation code executes. Results must be compared against these expectations; agreement and disagreement are both reportable.

red_first_discipline.description: A repair only counts after an observed failing check. Without it, 35% of successful repairs are vacuously green (test-after theater): the check stays broken but is masked from CI, QA, self-repair, the completion guard, and anchored review.
red_first_discipline.enters_formula_as: recovery factor in R(t); does not alter D(t) directly
red_first_discipline.calibration_prediction: OFF arms should widen the calibration gap (self-claimed pass exceeds objective pass).

reviewer_independence.description: Terminal review in a fresh context catches actually-broken checks at 0.75 (including masked/stale ones); anchored review catches only visibly-broken checks at 0.25. Caught checks get one bounded repair attempt.
reviewer_independence.calibration_prediction: ON arms should narrow the calibration gap by surfacing hidden breakage.

evidence_freshness.description: Trailing polish edits invalidate each green check with probability 0.12 after the last verify. With freshness ON a forced terminal re-verify reveals the breaks and gets one bounded repair pass; OFF, the completion claim uses the stale snapshot.
evidence_freshness.calibration_prediction: OFF arms should widen the calibration gap (stale evidence hides breaks from the claim).

doctrine_reinjection.description: Without reinjection the per-step error rate ramps linearly up to 1.8x by end of run (process amnesia / instruction drift). With it the rate stays flat.
doctrine_reinjection.enters_formula_as: recovery factor in R(t); modeled as suppressing a drift-driven error ramp
doctrine_reinjection.calibration_prediction: Little direct calibration effect; drift breaks are visible to downstream stages.

arms_note: full_pipeline = all core factors on; no_agentic_qa = agentic_qa and fix_loop off. Each factor is contrasted ON vs OFF with the other three discipline factors OFF and only its own mechanism knobs nonzero.

predictions.rationale: The full pipeline performs many repairs (self-repair plus fix loop); with 35% of repairs vacuous when OFF, masked checks accumulate and are unrecoverable by any later stage.
High stratum has the most breakage and therefore the most repair events exposed to the vacuous-green mechanism.
Without the QA/fix loop the only repairs are commit-time self-repairs, so fewer repair events are exposed to vacuous greens.
More breakage than medium but repairs remain limited to self-repair; effect bounded by repair volume.
Ceiling effect: the full pipeline leaves little residual breakage for any terminal reviewer to catch.
Some residual breakage survives the full pipeline on high tasks; an independent reviewer catches more of it than an anchored one.
Without QA the terminal review is the main recovery stage; tripling the catch rate should produce a clear positive delta.
Maximum residual breakage at review time; largest expected gain from independent review.
Polish edits strike after QA regardless of arm; with ~all checks green, expected recovery is roughly 0.12 x 0.65 of the green mass.
Slightly less green mass than medium but the same terminal mechanism applies.
Less green mass at polish time reduces the absolute recovery available to the re-verify.
Smallest green mass of the four cells; the stale mechanism has the least to invalidate and the re-verify the least to recover.
Drift-driven extra breakage is largely recovered by the QA/fix loop on medium tasks.
Recovery is closer to saturation on high tasks, so more drift breakage survives, but the pipeline still absorbs most of it.
Without the QA/fix loop, drift-driven breakage late in the run goes largely unrecovered.
Long runs amplify the ramp (more late steps at elevated error) and nothing downstream recovers the breakage.

claim_rule: Cite measured deltas from data/discipline_ablation.json only. If a measured delta is negligible, negative, or outside the predicted range, report that result as-is and do not claim improvement for that cell. All results are simulation-only; no live effect claims.
